summary.text: Bernard Quince is an independent candidate for Ripon at the 2026 election. The ABC describes him as a factory worker in Ararat who previously taught science at high school. He also ran in Ripon as an independent in 2022, receiving 0.7% of the primary vote.

occupation.text: Factory worker; former high school science teacher

sources.title: Ripon (VIC) 2026 election guide, ABC News
Candidates of the 2022 Victorian state election, Wikipedia

summary.text: Donna Buxton is the One Nation candidate for Ripon at the 2026 election. The ABC's candidate notes say she is a speech pathologist and small-business owner in Charlton who used to teach in primary schools. She has a business degree and postgraduate study in education; her One Nation candidate page could not be read for this profile.

occupation.text: Speech pathologist and small-business owner; former primary school teacher

sources.title: Ripon (VIC) 2026 election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Jeff Barry is the Libertarian candidate for Ripon at the 2026 election. Raised on a dairy farm in the Otways, he spent 35 years running his own tree-care business in Melbourne and has lived at Amphitheatre, near Avoca, for about three years. He is a CFA member and stood for the Libertarians in the federal seat of Mallee in 2025.

occupation.text: Arborist (ran his own arboriculture business in Melbourne for 35 years)

priorities.text: Cutting back state regulation of farmers and businesses

sources.title: Ripon (VIC) 2026 election guide, ABC News
Our state election candidates 2026, Libertarians Victoria
Results of the 2025 Australian federal election in Victoria, Wikipedia

summary.text: Jo Armstrong is the Nationals candidate for Ripon at the 2026 election. From Tatyoon, she has been an Ararat Rural City councillor since 2016, five years of that as mayor, and is state president of the Victorian Nationals. She topped the Ararat council poll in both 2020 and 2024.

prior_roles.note: The ABC says she has spent five years as mayor but gives no years and doesn't say whether she still holds the post.

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC says she has been on the council since 2016; no source read gives the label she ran under.
Wikipedia's results table lists her as an Independent National.
Wikipedia's results table lists her as an Independent National.

priorities.text: Better roads across the electorate
Easier access to health services
Housing that local people can afford
Opposing the Emergency Services levy
More transparency and less corruption in government

summary.text: Mark McGrath is the Family First candidate for Ripon at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. summary.text: Martha Haylett has been the Labor MP for Ripon since 2022, when she defeated the sitting Liberal member Louise Staley. Her earlier career covered housing affordability, job support and transport for country Victorians. She became Parliamentary Secretary for Rural and Regional Development in August 2026 and is recontesting Ripon in 2026.

occupation.text: Housing, employment support and regional transport

prior_roles.role: Parliamentary Secretary for Rural and Regional Development
prior_roles.note: Wikipedia words the title as Regional and Rural Development; the title here is Parliament's.

priorities.text: Stronger health care in rural and regional areas
More affordable housing
Wider access to mental health services in the regions
Opportunities for young people through education and jobs
Repairing roads across Ripon

sources.title: Martha Haylett, Parliament of Victoria
Martha Haylett, Wikipedia

summary.text: Megan Read is the Liberal candidate for Ripon at the 2026 election. Born in Creswick and raised in Ballarat, she lives on and runs her family's farm near Beaufort, and set up her own business, Ballarat Myotherapy, at 21. She has been president of a local kindergarten, a school parents club and a working group on childcare, and has campaigned on how renewable energy infrastructure is rolled out in the region.

occupation.text: Manages her family farm; founder of Ballarat Myotherapy

prior_roles.note: The ABC says she started the business at 21; no source says whether she still runs it.

priorities.text: A fairer deal for communities hosting renewable energy infrastructure
Abolishing the Emergency Services and Volunteers Fund levy
Support for families recovering from the Streatham-Skipton bushfire

sources.title: Ripon (VIC) 2026 election guide, ABC News
Megan Read, Liberal for Ripon, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Taylah Brennan-Jones is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Ripon at the 2026 election. She works full-time as a job coach for people with disability and also teaches swimming. She takes part in an Ararat community project aimed at creating more events and opportunities for young people in the region.

occupation.text: Job coach for people with disability and swim teacher

priorities.text: Fully funded, accessible regional healthcare
Public and affordable housing
More public transport routes in rural and regional areas
Greater public investment in local services

sources.title: Ripon (VIC) 2026 election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Tim Drylie is the Greens candidate for Ripon at the 2026 election. He has been a Hepburn Shire councillor since the November 2020 election, was re-elected in 2024 and is a former mayor of the shire. He has worked on cutting emissions, including within local government in Bendigo, and now helps households and small businesses lower their energy bills.

occupation.text: Helps households and small businesses cut energy costs; formerly in emissions reduction work, including in Bendigo local government

prior_roles.organisation: A local business and tourism group

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC says he was elected in November 2020; no source read gives the ward or the label he ran under.

priorities.text: Affordable housing
Better health, education and aged care services
Safe, inclusive communities free from violence
Climate action that benefits regional Victoria

sources.title: Ripon (VIC) 2026 election guide, ABC News
